problem: Dataset distillation struggles to simultaneously achieve diversity, generalization, and representativeness in synthesized datasets without external constraints.
approach: The method quantifies representativeness using a Mercer kernel to measure similarity between synthetic and real data in feature space, then guides the reverse diffusion process with this prior without retraining.
contribution: DAP outperforms state-of-the-art methods on ImageNet-1K and achieves superior cross-architecture generalization in dataset distillation.

problem: Current transformer-based LLMs have quadratic compute and linear memory bottlenecks that limit inference efficiency, while linear-scaling models lack capabilities or hardware efficiency.
approach: Mamba-3 combines three improvements inspired by state-space models: more expressive recurrence, complex state update rules for richer tracking, and multi-input/output formulation to better exploit hardware parallelism during decoding.
contribution: Mamba-3 achieves significant gains in retrieval, state-tracking, and language modeling tasks, setting the Pareto frontier for performance under fixed inference budget.

problem: Existing unlearnable example methods rely on empirical heuristics without solid theoretical explanations, making them difficult to improve systematically.
approach: The work analyzes unlearnable examples from a mutual information reduction perspective, showing effective methods decrease mutual information between clean and poisoned features, then proposes MI-UE that maximizes cosine similarity among intra-class features to reduce covariance.
contribution: MI-UE significantly outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods in preventing unauthorized model learning even under defense mechanisms.

problem: Open-set test-time adaptation for 3D point cloud semantic segmentation is hindered by class imbalance where known samples dominate and unknown instances are sparse or absent.
approach: GOOD leverages geometric priors to cluster point clouds into superpoints, introduces a confidence metric to distinguish known and unknown points, and uses prototype-based representations for robust segmentation.
contribution: GOOD outperforms HGL by 1.93% mIoU, 8.99% AUROC, and 7.91% FPR95 on the Synth4D to SemanticKITTI benchmark.

problem: Peer review integrity is threatened by the potential use of LLMs to generate negligent reviews, yet there is no comprehensive resource for benchmarking AI text detection in this domain.
approach: The work introduces a dataset of 788,984 AI-written peer reviews paired with human reviews from ICLR and NeurIPS, then evaluates 18 AI text detection algorithms and proposes Anchor, a context-aware method leveraging manuscript content.
contribution: The evaluation reveals the difficulty of identifying AI-generated peer reviews at the individual level, highlighting the urgent need for better detection tools.

problem: Designing effective multi-agent systems requires optimizing both prompts and topologies, which is inherently complex and difficult to automate.
approach: MASS is a three-stage optimization framework that interleaves local prompt optimization, workflow topology optimization, and global prompt optimization, where each stage is conditioned on iteratively optimized components from former stages.
contribution: MASS-optimized systems substantially outperform existing alternatives and reveal design principles for building effective multi-agent systems.

problem: Anisotropic singular value spectra in parameters, activations, and gradients cause wide numerical ranges that introduce quantization bias and spectral distortion, severely degrading low-bit training of LLMs.
approach: Metis partitions anisotropic spectra into narrower sub-distributions for independent quantization using random sampling and projection, leveraging properties of the dominant spectral subspace to minimize decomposition overhead.
contribution: Metis enables robust W4A4G4 FP4 training of LLaMA-3 8B with only 0.4% training loss gap and 0.1% downstream accuracy degradation relative to BF16.

problem: Vision-language models struggle to simultaneously express hierarchy within concept families and compositionality across different concept families.
approach: PHyCLIP employs an l1-product metric on a Cartesian product of hyperbolic factors, with intra-family hierarchies emerging in individual hyperbolic factors and cross-family composition captured by the l1-product metric.
contribution: PHyCLIP outperforms single-space approaches on zero-shot classification, retrieval, hierarchical classification, and compositional understanding tasks with more interpretable embedding structures.

problem: Existing vision-language and audio models cannot reliably converse with users in real-time about live scenes, despite advances in individual modalities.
approach: The work introduces the Interactive Video Dataset (IVD) that assesses how well existing models support real-time question-answering based on camera and audio input, and shows fine-tuning on this data reduces performance gaps.
contribution: IVD reveals that existing models fall far behind human performance and identifies main sources of performance gaps, while showing fine-tuning can significantly reduce the gap.

problem: Cross-modal representation learning optimizes statistical objectives without causal constraints, introducing spurious dependencies and representation-induced structural drift that undermines causal inference.
approach: CARL explicitly embeds causal structure preservation constraints using multi-consistency loss architecture with conditional independence preservation, information bottleneck regularization, and Markov boundary preservation loss.
contribution: CARL achieves state-of-the-art performance in preserving conditional independence patterns under synthetic experiments with known causal ground truth.

problem: Enabling LLMs for open-ended and mechanistic reasoning in biology is hindered because most biological outcomes are non-verifiable, limiting application of Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards.
approach: CellDuality uses a complementary task duality principle where the model performs forward reasoning (predicting biological outcomes) followed by inverse reasoning (reconstructing initial conditions), with reconstruction fidelity serving as intrinsic reward without ground-truth labels.
contribution: CellDuality enables LLM agents for robust reasoning in single-cell biology through self-supervised feedback without verifiable rewards.

problem: Online conformal prediction methods produce overly conservative prediction sets under data distribution shifts in fully adversarial environments.
approach: COP incorporates underlying data patterns into the update rule through estimated cumulative distribution functions of non-conformity scores, producing tighter prediction sets when predictable patterns exist while maintaining valid coverage.
contribution: COP achieves valid coverage guarantees and constructs shorter prediction intervals than baseline methods while achieving finite-sample coverage under arbitrary learning rates.

problem: Multimodal LLMs struggle to understand humans in diverse, complex scenarios at multiple levels of perception, comprehension, and reasoning.
approach: HumanPCR is an evaluation suite with over 6,000 multiple-choice questions across perception and comprehension levels, plus manually curated video reasoning tests requiring integration of visual evidence and proactive context extraction.
contribution: Extensive evaluation of 30+ state-of-the-art models reveals significant challenges in human-centric visual understanding, especially in spatial perception, temporal understanding, and mind modeling.

problem: Instruction-based image editing applies uniform generation processes across entire images despite edited and unedited regions having significantly different generation difficulty and computational needs.
approach: RegionE adaptively partitions images into edited and unedited regions, applies one-step prediction to unedited areas and local iterative denoising to edited regions, using Region-Instruction KV Cache and adaptive velocity decay cache.
contribution: RegionE accelerates image editing tasks without additional training while maintaining high quality.

problem: Existing symmetry-based disentanglement requires strong prior knowledge of symmetry group structure or restrictive assumptions about subgroup properties.
approach: The method enables embodied agents to autonomously discover group structure through unsupervised interaction with the environment, with proven identifiability under minimal assumptions.
contribution: The approach outperforms existing Linear Symmetry-Based Disentangled (LSBD) methods on three environments with different group decompositions.

problem: Q-value biases in offline-to-online RL follow heavy-tailed distributions during online fine-tuning, causing high estimation variance and hindering performance improvement.
approach: LAROO introduces parameterized Laplace-distributed noise to transfer heavy-tailed bias nature into the noise, combines estimated Q-values with noise, and uses conservative ensemble-based estimates to re-center biases.
contribution: LAROO achieves significant performance improvement over baselines by promoting heavy-tailed Q-value biases into a standardized form.

problem: Multimodal large language models struggle with complex mathematical reasoning despite impressive capabilities in other domains.
approach: WE-MATH 2.0 integrates a structured mathematical knowledge hierarchy with 491 knowledge points, model-centric data space modeling with diverse difficulty levels, and a two-stage RL framework combining supervised fine-tuning and progressive alignment RL.
contribution: WE-MATH 2.0 achieves competitive performance on widely used benchmarks while demonstrating strong generalization on a comprehensive benchmark covering all 491 knowledge points.

problem: Existing consistent approaches for partial and complementary multi-label learning either require accurate estimation of label generation processes or make unrealistic uniform distribution assumptions.
approach: The work proposes risk estimators based on first- and second-order strategies that handle both partial and complementary multi-label learning in a unified way without relying on aforementioned conditions.
contribution: The approach proves consistency with respect to two widely used multi-label classification metrics and derives convergence rates for estimation errors.

problem: Time Series Foundation Models designed for real-valued series cannot effectively leverage heterogeneous covariates like categorical variables and multimodal data, which are task-specific and unavailable during pretraining.
approach: UniCA performs covariate homogenization to transform heterogeneous covariates into high-level homogeneous series representations, then fuses them via unified attention-based mechanism while preserving TSFM generalization.
contribution: UniCA demonstrates superiority on multiple unimodal and multimodal covariate-aware forecasting benchmarks.

problem: Acquiring fine-grained, high-resolution time series data is often limited by cost and feasibility, necessitating super-resolution from sparse, low-resolution inputs.
approach: SRT decomposes input into trend and seasonal components, aligns them to target resolution using implicit neural representation, and leverages cross-resolution attention to guide high-resolution detail generation via disentangled rectified flow.
contribution: SRT and SRT-large consistently outperform existing methods across nine public datasets at multiple scale factors with strong zero-shot super-resolution capability.

problem: Speech synthesis models lack alignment with human perception due to the absence of large-scale human preference datasets, particularly for naturalness.
approach: SpeechJudge introduces a comprehensive suite with 99k human feedback speech pairs, establishes a challenging benchmark for speech naturalness judgment, and develops a generative reward model using Qwen2.5-Omni-7B trained via SFT and RL with GRPO.
contribution: SpeechJudge-GRM achieves 77.2% accuracy on the SpeechJudge-Eval benchmark, substantially improving over existing metrics and AudioLLMs.

problem: Activation sparsity benefits in ReLU models do not directly apply to modern LLMs, resulting in fragmented model-specific strategies and limited general understanding.
approach: The work introduces a framework for evaluating sparsity robustness in contemporary LLMs and conducts systematic investigation of activation sparsity in feedforward layers across diverse model families and scales.
contribution: Results uncover universal properties of activation sparsity across diverse models and scales, showing potential for effective sparsity grows with model size, with first study of activation sparsity in diffusion-based LLMs.

problem: Joint Energy-Based Models for simultaneous robust classification and high-fidelity generation suffer from training instability and poor sample quality from SGLD-based approaches.
approach: The method integrates adversarial training principles by replacing SGLD-based learning with stable AT-based approach using Binary Cross-Entropy loss, combines adversarial training for robustness with gradient regularization, and employs two-stage training to address normalization instabilities.
contribution: The approach is the first EBM-based hybrid to scale to high-resolution datasets (ImageNet 256x256) with high training stability while achieving state-of-the-art discriminative and generative performance.

problem: Single-view metric depth estimation from sparse observations requires complex architectural designs to generate metric-accurate dense depth maps.
approach: LDCM uses a Poisson-based depth initialization module to generate coarse dense depth from diverse sparse observations as a structural prior, replaces depth head with point map head for direct 3D coordinate regression, and eliminates camera intrinsic dependency.
contribution: LDCM consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple benchmarks and sparsity levels with strong generalization to unseen data distributions.

problem: The counting power of transformers remains unclear beyond semi-linear properties expressible as boolean combinations of linear inequalities.
approach: The work provides formal framework proving transformers can capture semialgebraic counting properties expressible as boolean combinations of arbitrary multivariate polynomials, with connections to Hilbert's tenth problem showing undecidability results.
contribution: Results demonstrate transformers can express highly nonlinear counting properties generalizing those capturable by support vector machines with polynomial kernels.

problem: Existing benchmarks for evaluating long-range capabilities in graph learning cannot guarantee tasks depend on long-range information or are too limited, making claims of improvement questionable.
approach: LRIM introduces a physics-based benchmark using the Ising model with provably long-range dependencies, consisting of ten datasets scaling from 256 to 65k nodes with controllable long-range interactions through tunable parameters.
contribution: Experiments show both message-passing architectures and graph transformers perform far from optimal, especially scalable methods, providing model-agnostic evidence that local information is insufficient.

problem: Imputing missing values in multivariate time series is challenging under diverse missing patterns and heavy missingness because corrupted temporal features hinder cross-variable information transfer.
approach: T1 uses a CNN-Transformer hybrid with Channel-Head Binding creating one-to-one correspondence between CNN channels and attention heads, enabling selective information transfer where affected pathways down-weight based on observable patterns.
contribution: T1 achieves state-of-the-art performance, reducing MSE by 46% on average compared to the second-best baseline with particularly strong gains under extreme sparsity (70% missing ratio).

problem: Streaming video generation suffers from severe error accumulation over long horizons, significantly degrading quality in interactive world models and neural game engines.
approach: Rolling Forcing uses joint denoising of multiple frames with progressively increasing noise levels, integrates attention sink mechanism for global context anchoring, and employs efficient training algorithm with few-step distillation over extended windows.
contribution: Rolling Forcing enables real-time streaming generation of multi-minute videos on a single GPU with substantially reduced error accumulation.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models benefit from chain-of-thought reasoning but long output generation for thoughts negatively affects inference time in real-world robotic tasks.
approach: HyT enables VLAs to learn from thoughts and benefit from performance gains while optionally omitting CoT generation during inference, supporting flexible conditional prediction of diverse outputs.
contribution: HyT preserves performance improvements from reasoning without the inference time cost through hybrid training.

problem: All-in-one image restoration requires approximating heterogeneous inverse functions from diverse mixed degradations, yet principles governing effective restoration remain underexplored.
approach: The work revisits attention mechanisms for all-in-one restoration, identifying two bottlenecks: linear value paths restricting expressivity and absence of explicit global slot for degradation context, proposing nonlinear value transform and global spatial token.
contribution: Proposed primitives improve restoration across synthetic, mixed, underwater, and medical benchmarks with negligible overhead and consistent performance gains.

problem: Model-based offline RL relies on dynamics models for policy exploration and evaluation, but many exhibit limited capability in long-horizon prediction due to error accumulation.
approach: ADM-v2 structurally decouples recurrent forward of RNN cells from backtracked state, making direct prediction more flexible and supporting parallel uncertainty estimation, enabling full-horizon roll-outs.
contribution: ADM-v2 achieves SOTA on both D4RL and NeoRL under full-horizon roll-out setting, with substantial advancements for policy optimization while other models degrade.

problem: Current approaches to decoding visual representations from brain signals emphasize high-level semantic features while neglecting pixel-level details, limiting understanding of human visual system.
approach: The work leverages multiple pre-trained visual encoders with distinct inductive biases to capture hierarchical visual representations using contrastive learning objective, introducing a Fusion Prior that learns stable mapping from large-scale data.
contribution: The method achieves favorable balance between retrieval accuracy and reconstruction fidelity through hierarchical visual embedding alignment.

problem: Automating mathematical formalization for theorem proving is hindered because informal statements are complex and offer limited context on underlying math concepts for effective retrieval.
approach: DRIFT enables LLMs to decompose informal mathematical statements into smaller sub-components for targeted premise retrieval from libraries like Mathlib, and retrieves illustrative theorems to help models use premises more effectively.
contribution: DRIFT consistently improves premise retrieval nearly doubling F1 score compared to DPR baseline on ProofNet with strong performance on out-of-distribution ConNF benchmark.

problem: Evaluating AI agents on complex, open-ended deep research tasks is hindered by lack of realistic benchmarks that include both public and private knowledge sources.
approach: DRBench introduces a benchmark with 100 tasks across 10 domains that require identifying supporting facts from public web and private company knowledge bases, grounded in realistic user personas and enterprise context.
contribution: Evaluation of diverse agents on DRBench demonstrates their strengths and weaknesses, highlighting critical paths for advancing enterprise deep research.

problem: Neural networks implicitly learn class-specific functional modules but cannot be easily isolated and recombined for modular inference.
approach: The method trains sparse networks with KL-divergence-based loss to learn only functional modules for assigned class subsets, using iterative magnitude pruning to remove irrelevant weights, enabling composition via weight summation or logit averaging.
contribution: Trained subnetworks achieve high accuracy on target classes with minimal leakage, and combined modules often recover generalist performance with interpretable functional structure.

problem: Existing multimodal Process Reward Models lack sufficient training data to effectively estimate step-wise value scores during reasoning.
approach: The work constructs VisualPRM400K with 400K multimodal process supervision data to develop VisualPRM capable of estimating value scores for each step, with VisualProcessBench for measuring PRM and MLLM abilities.
contribution: VisualPRM improves reasoning performance of three types of MLLMs with 5.9-point improvement on seven benchmarks even when applied to highly capable models like InternVL2.5-78B.

problem: Off-policy RL systems with stale rollout data either degrade in performance or collapse during training, limiting efficiency and scalability of LLM reasoning.
approach: M2PO constrains the second moment of importance weights to suppress extreme outliers while preserving informative updates, reducing clipped high-variance tokens while maintaining stable optimization.
contribution: M2PO delivers stable off-policy training even with data stale by at least 256 model updates, matching on-policy performance across six model scales and eight reasoning benchmarks.

problem: State-of-the-art data-driven models systematically underestimate magnitudes and short-term variations of extreme wind velocities despite performing well for general meteorological forecasting.
approach: The work provides theoretical analysis of how data frequency spectrum influences extreme wind prediction errors, proposes novel loss function with gradient penalty and frequency reweighting in physics-embedded machine learning models.
contribution: The approach achieves significant improvements in extreme wind velocity prediction while maintaining robust overall performance.

problem: Unified multimodal models with shared transformers suffer from severe gradient conflicts between vision and text due to different statistical properties of images and text.
approach: Uni-X proposes a two-end-separated, middle-shared X-shaped architecture dedicating initial and final layers to modality-specific processing while maintaining shared middle layers for high-level semantic fusion.
contribution: Uni-X achieves superior training efficiency and at 3B parameters matches or surpasses 7B AR-based UMMs with GenEval score of 82 for image generation and strong vision/text performance.

problem: Speculative decoding relies on static time allocation between drafting and verification, while dynamic approaches optimize proxy metrics like acceptance length rather than actual throughput.
approach: LTD formulates the problem as a reinforcement learning environment training two co-adaptive policies to dynamically coordinate draft and verification phases, directly optimizing throughput.
contribution: LTD achieves speedup ratios of 2.24x to 4.32x across five LLMs and four tasks, outperforming Eagle3 by up to 36.4%.
